content.text:
I'm mapping out the grid values row by row, tracking which cells hold which numbers to identify the distinct components.

Now I'm tracing connectivity between same-numbered cells: the 6s form three separate groups, the 9s form two diagonal chains, and the 3s and 7s each split into separate clusters depending on adjacency, including diagonal connections.

For the 2s I find two groups (comp J and comp K), and for the 8s I identify four separate components (L, M, N, O) based on checking adjacency between rows. Now I'm ready to start pairing these components up.

Moving to color 6, I have three groups: A along row0, B along col9, and C along row6. Checking connections, A and C share column 2, giving a vertical link between them at rows 1-5, while A-B and B-C have no shared rows or columns.

For color 9, I have D forming a diagonal in rows 2-4 and E forming a diagonal in rows 6-9, and I'm checking whether their rows overlap to determine if they connect.

On columns 3 and 4, I find col4 gives the smaller gap (rows 4-5), so I'll draw the vertical connector there.

For color 3, F sits on row2 and G on col6, sharing column 6, so I'll fill rows 3-5 in col6 to link them.

Now I'm starting to trace color 7's groups, H running diagonally and I running vertically down column 5.

Checking row6, both shapes meet with H at column9 and I at column5, so I'll connect them horizontally across columns 6-8.

Color 2's groups sit far apart in both rows and columns with no shared line, so no connector applies there.

Now I'm moving on to color 8, identifying its scattered shapes across rows 1, 5, and 7-8.

Comparing L and O I find a shared column 7, filling rows 2-8 vertically, while M and N share column 1, needing just the single cell at row 6. M-O and N-O don't align on any shared row or column, so no connectors there.

Now I'm assembling the final 10x10 grid, marking all the connector cells: column 2 rows 1-5, column 4 rows 4-5, column 6 rows 3-5, row 6 across columns 6-8, column 7 rows 2-8, and the single cell at row 6 column 1, laying out each row accordingly.

content.text:
I'm checking colors 9 and 1, which each have only a single connected shape, so those can be skipped. For color 7, I'm examining two shapes at columns 5-6 and 6-7 to see if there's a gap between them that would connect the components.

For color 8, shapes at rows 6-8 and row 8 have a horizontal gap at row 8 spanning columns 3-6, which is where gray connectors get drawn. For color 2, shapes near rows 9-12 share row 11, giving a gap at columns 5-8 for the connector, even though some of those cells already contain 7s in the input.
